raw_response:
I farm the same 7.5 mu the way we have for years, wheat first, then maize right after. I do not have much room to take risks on such a small piece of land, so I mostly follow what has worked on my fields and what the other families around here do. Wheat and maize together keep things steady. We have well water, so if the rain is short I can still save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not water more than needed. Some people from my family work outside, so at busy times I depend on the people at home and try to keep the work simple and on time.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, not too late, with the seed we usually buy locally. Before sowing I will put on a base fertilizer, not too little because if wheat stays yellow later, yield drops badly. Then I will topdress once around jointing if the seedlings look like they need strength. I will water a few times, mainly after sowing if the soil is dry, around overwintering or turning green, and around jointing or grain filling depending on rain. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry and plant maize right away. That gap is short, so I will do light rotary tillage or direct planting after clearing straw, whichever is easier to arrange. For maize I will use hybrid seed from the local dealer, put some fertilizer at planting, and then one more time when it gets taller. Usually maize here does not need as much water as wheat if summer rain comes, but if it turns dry I will give one or two irrigations. I only spray pesticide when I actually see weeds or insects, because every bottle costs money.
